subproblem.title: Directional derivatives of a locally Lipschitz function along a differentiable chart (Simon Ch. 2, 4.10)
subproblem.statement: Let n, P ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^P → ℝ, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and w ∈ ℝⁿ. Assume F is Lipschitz (with some constant K ≥ 0) on some neighbourhood V of Φ(w), Φ is differentiable at w and F∘Φ is differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the function t ↦ F(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)s at t = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n P : ℕ) (F : Eucl P → ℝ) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (w : Eucl n), (∃ K : ℝ≥0, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 (Φ w), LipschitzOnWith K F V) → DifferentiableAt ℝ Φ w → DifferentiableAt ℝ (F ∘ Φ) w → ∀ s : Eucl n, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => F (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (F ∘ Φ) w s) 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. ℝ^k = Eucl k with norm |·|; DΦ(w) := fderiv ℝ Φ w and D(F∘Φ)(w) := fderiv ℝ (F ∘ Φ) w. “F is K-Lipschitz on V” means |F(y) − F(z)| ≤ K|y − z| for all y, z ∈ V. o(t) denotes a function of t ∈ ℝ that is little-o of t as t → 0.
Source. Simon Ch. 2, 4.7 and 4.10 (directional derivatives of a Lipschitz function along a differentiable chart). This is the real-valued form of the argument in the parent proof's Step 3. For small |t| both Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) lie in V, so |F(Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s) − F(Φ(w + ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w + ts)| = o(t), while F(Φ(w + ts)) = F(Φ(w)) + t·D(F∘Φ)(w)s + o(t).

Alternative route. The comparator-accepted DAG lemma lpf_ccr_hasDerivAt_line_of_comp is the same statement for Eucl Q-valued maps. The present statement follows by applying it with Q := 1 to x ↦ EuclideanSpace.single 0 (F x) (an isometric embedding ℝ → Eucl 1 composed with F) and reading off coordinate 0. A decomposition of this node may reuse it. The direct proof is as follows.

Let K, V be as in the hypothesis: V ∈ 𝓝(Φ(w)) and F is K-Lipschitz on V. Fix s ∈ ℝⁿ. Put x := Φ(w), v := DΦ(w)s, b := D(F∘Φ)(w)s, g₁(t) := F(x + t v), g₂(t) := F(Φ(w + t s)) and q := g₁ − g₂ (t ∈ ℝ).

1. (Derivatives along the line.) The affine line ℓ(t) := w + t s has ℓ(0) = w and derivative s at t = 0.
 - Φ is differentiable at w = ℓ(0), so by the chain rule (`HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt`) t ↦ Φ(w + t s) has derivative DΦ(w)s = v at t = 0.
 - F∘Φ is differentiable at w, so likewise g₂ = (F∘Φ)∘ℓ has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)s = b at t = 0.

2. (First-order expansion of Φ along the line.) By step 1 and the little-o characterization of derivatives (`hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO`), using Φ(w + 0·s) = x: Φ(w + t s) − x − t v = o(t) as t → 0.

3. (Both points eventually lie in V.) As t → 0, x + t v → x, and Φ(w + t s) → Φ(w) = x because t ↦ Φ(w + t s) is differentiable, hence continuous, at 0. Since V is a neighbourhood of x, there is a neighbourhood of t = 0 on which x + t v ∈ V and Φ(w + t s) ∈ V. For such t, because F is K-Lipschitz on V,
 |q(t)| = |F(x + t v) − F(Φ(w + t s))| ≤ K|x + t v − Φ(w + t s)| = K|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|.

4. (q has derivative 0 at 0.) By step 3, q(t) = O(|Φ(w + t s) − x − t v|) as t → 0, and by step 2 the latter is o(t). Hence q(t) = o(t) (`Asymptotics.IsBigO.trans_isLittleO`). Moreover q(0) = F(x) − F(Φ(w)) = 0. So q(t) − q(0) − t·0 = o(t), i.e. q has derivative 0 at t = 0 (`hasDerivAt_iff_isLittleO`).

5. (Conclusion.) g₁ = g₂ + q pointwise. By steps 1 and 4 and the sum rule (`HasDerivAt.add`), g₁ has derivative b + 0 = b at t = 0, that is, HasDerivAt (fun t => F (Φ w + t • fderiv ℝ Φ w s)) (fderiv ℝ (F ∘ Φ) w s) 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: t ↦ Φ(w+ts) has derivative DΦ(w)s and t ↦ F(Φ(w+ts)) has derivative D(F∘Φ)(w)s at 0 (chain rule).
For small t both Φ(w) + t DΦ(w)s and Φ(w+ts) lie in V, so the difference of the two functions is ≤ K·o(t).
Hence the difference has derivative 0 at 0, and the sum rule gives the claim.

audit.reason: The proof correctly obtains eventual membership of both comparison curves in the Lipschitz neighbourhood. Their difference is little-o of t, so its derivative is zero; the chain and sum rules give precisely the stated derivative without ambient differentiability of F.
